capacity_usable_kwh.notes: EV Database: 28 kWh usable (marked estimated there) of 30 kWh nominal. No Nissan page states a usable figure.

capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Press kit says "30 kWh" laminated lithium-ion (bare capacity, taken as gross).

chemistry.notes: EV Database lists an NMC cathode for the 30 kWh pack; Nissan only says "revised chemistry". The 24 kWh pack of the same generation is LMO per DOE, so this is uncertain.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: EV Database: 400 V architecture, nominal about 350 V (96S).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: EV Database states battery preconditioning is not supported (or "No") for this pack. Nissan US press kits (2012, 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2024) describe only remote cabin heating/cooling (NissanConnect EV) and, in 2012-2014, a cold-weather battery heater that warms the pack while charging; none describes a navigation or manual battery-warming-before-charging feature. Nissan's navigation-linked battery heater first appears on the third-generation LEAF.

dc_max_kw.notes: EV Database (30 kWh, MY15-17): max DC 47 kW (10-80 % average 45 kW). No Nissan page states a kW figure for this pack.

ac_max_kw.notes: 2016 US press kit: SV 6.6 kW standard (6.0 kW output). Convention: the onboard-charger rating as Nissan prints it for that year (3.3 kW in the 2011-12 sheets; 3.6 kW rating / 3.3 kW output on later US S sheets; 6.6 kW rating / 6.0 kW output).
